result:
`bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (7 tests, 3 files) both pass.

The bug was entirely in `ProfileController.update` (`app/Http/Controllers/ProfileController.ts`): it read the request body raw via `this.request.json<ProfileInput>()` with no validation, then wrote it through `User.forceUpdate` with a spread of the whole body — which both skipped the name/email rules and bypassed mass-assignment protection, letting arbitrary keys like `id` and `passwordHash` reach the row. The project already had an unused `ProfileUpdateSchema` in `app/Http/Validators/ProfileValidator.ts` encoding exactly the required rules (name trimmed/required/≤120, email required/lowercased/well-formed, password optional but ≥8 when non-empty), so I wired the controller back to it with `this.validateBody(ProfileUpdateSchema)` — which raises a 422 `ValidationException` keyed by field, the shape `resources/js/pages/profile/Edit.tsx` already renders — and swapped `User.forceUpdate` for `User.update`, so writes go through the model's `fillable: ['name', 'email', 'password']` list and non-form fields are dropped rather than persisted. The valid-update path, the email-uniqueness check, and the session refresh are unchanged. I also added `tests/ProfileController.test.ts`, a DB-backed feature test covering the valid update (including lowercasing), rejection of a malformed email, an empty name, and a too-short password (each asserting the account row is untouched), and that an `id`/`passwordHash` sent alongside valid fields is ignored while the valid fields still save.
